messages.author: 9fe983a15f9899f9
messages.subject: MLR/WLSMV and within-subjects covariance matrix
parts:
Hello lavaan community,

I would like to fit a CFA for Likert-type data (range: 1 - 7). I have multiple observations per subject.

To account for the multilevel structure, I would like to fit the model to the within-subjects covariance matrix. I know how to calculate that by hand in R. I would then simply provide it to the cfa() function via the sample.cov argument. Since all my variables are on level 1 (i.e., no subject-level variables), a full multilevel-CFA is not required, as far as I understand.

Since my data is ordinal, MLR or WLSMV estimation seem appropriate. However, I have read that WLSMV (and also MLR?) is based on polychoric or tetrachoric correlations.

Would WLSMV/MLR conflict with the use of a within-subjects covariance matrix that is not calculated as polychoric? And more general, is my strategy appropriate?

I would be happy if someone could help. Thanks alot!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MLR/WLSMV and within-subjects covariance matrix
parts:
WLSMV is an analysis of polychoric correlations among latent responses.  MLR treats the discrete 1-7 scale as numeric rather than categorical.  The results are not directly comparable because the latent-response scale is arbitrary, but the standardized ("scale-free") solution will be practically the same with as many as 7 response categories.

https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/a0029315

I would be wary of cluster-mean centering.  At least be aware of the potential bias due to unreliability at both levels:

https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/a0024376

If you research questions all concern L1, you could just request cluster-robust SEs and tests by specifying your cluster= variable for a single-level model.  That is available with MLR.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Is there any citation that it would be justified to fit a single-level model this way?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MLR/WLSMV and within-subjects covariance matrix
parts: Your recommendation would be to use MLR (given that I have 7 categories) and simply specify the cluster argument without specifying different levels in the model syntax?
Is there any citation that it would be justified to fit a single-level model this way?

I linked to an article demonstrating 7-category ordinal data yield equivalent standardized solutions and similar test results using WLSMV and MLR:

https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/a0029315

This paper discusses the use of marginal rather than multilevel linear models.  SEM is a multivariate extension, so the same principles apply, but you can search for cluster-robust SEM literature as well.

https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/met0000078
